title: UNAM Students March Through CDMX on CCH Naucalpan Second Anniversary
detail: UNAM students marched through central Mexico City on May 8 — the second anniversary of a police intervention at CCH Naucalpan campus — demanding an end to violence and repression at public universities. The march proceeded along Insurgentes, Paseo de la Reforma, and surrounding arteries, causing significant traffic disruptions. Demonstrators called for accountability for the police action and raised broader demands around campus security, freedom from intimidation, and protection of student rights under the UNAM charter. The march is part of a recurring wave of student mobilization at Mexico's largest public university, which enrolls approximately 350,000 students across the metropolitan area.

title: Eight-Plus Simultaneous Demonstrations Converge on CDMX on May 8
detail: At least eight separate demonstrations took place across Mexico City on May 8, reflecting the breadth of civic mobilization in the capital. Confirmed marches included: the UNAM student march (CCH Naucalpan anniversary), CFE retirees demanding pension rights, the second anniversary march of the 'Convención de la CDMX' (housing and citizen rights, marching from Monumento a la Revolución to the Zócalo), an anti-fracking coalition march, and multiple recreational cycling events. Authorities tracked 3 formal marches, 14 separate concentrations, and 20 recreational events that day. Multiple central arteries including Insurgentes, Reforma, and Circuito Interior experienced congestion. Mexico City hosts more public demonstrations per capita than any other city in Latin America, averaging more than 4,000 protests annually.

title: Metro Line 5 Partial Closure; Motorcyclist Killed in Metrobús Collision
detail: Several Metro Line 5 stations between Hangares and Terminal Aérea were suspended on May 7–8 due to a guide bar fault caused by thermal expansion during the ongoing heat wave. The STC deployed provisional bus bridge service (puente vial) to cover the affected stretch, adding to surface traffic delays alongside multiple marches. Separately, on May 8, a motorcyclist died after colliding with a Metrobús articulated unit at Circuito Cuemanco station in Xochimilco. The Metrobús network carries approximately 1.2 million passengers per day and has faced recurring safety concerns about conflicts with motorcyclists and private vehicles at exclusive busway intersections. Rain during the same period also disrupted Line 12 service, adding to Friday commuter congestion.
